genZNote: The only ciliate that bothers parasitizing humans, and the biggest protozoan parasite you'll ever meet.

morphology.shape: Large, ovoid trophozoite covered in cilia; spherical cyst
morphology.size: Trophozoites ~50-200 µm long — the largest protozoan parasite known to infect humans

protozoanDetails.lifeCycleForm: Trophozoite (motile, ciliated, invasive form) and cyst (environmentally resistant, infective form)

habitat.naturalHabitat: Large intestine of pigs (the primary natural host/reservoir) and, less commonly, humans
habitat.hostAssociation: Zoonotic — pigs are the main reservoir; human infection is relatively uncommon
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Cysts can persist in water/soil contaminated with pig feces
habitat.reservoir: Pigs; contaminated water in areas with close human-pig contact

microscopy.stain: Wet mount or iodine stain of stool
microscopy.appearance: Large, ciliated, ovoid trophozoites, easily visible even at low magnification given their size; spherical cysts also seen

identificationClues: Largest protozoan parasite of humans — trophozoites are visible even under low-power microscopy
Covered in cilia, unlike amoebae or flagellates seen in stool exams
History of close contact with pigs or pig-contaminated water is a classic epidemiologic clue

diseases: Balantidiasis — usually asymptomatic or mild diarrhea; occasionally dysentery with colonic ulceration resembling amebic dysentery in more severe cases
clinicalImportance.transmission: Fecal-oral, via ingestion of cysts from water or food contaminated with pig feces
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Relatively rare human infection worldwide; most common where humans live in close contact with pigs and sanitation is limited
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Its large size and ciliated surface make it one of the easier intestinal parasites to identify on a stool wet mount, once considered in the differential

examFacts.importantTest: Stool wet mount/iodine stain showing large ciliated trophozoites
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: The only ciliate known to parasitize humans, and the largest protozoan parasite of humans overall
